subject: Claimed 03:15 UTC stream silence — triage summary
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@acmeretail.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.example; marissa.cole@redwood.example
Date: 2027-10-07T03:18:12Z
Subject: Observed ~90s silence on streaming completions (03:15–03:17 UTC)

Hi team,

We saw a production incident early this morning where a live streaming completion for account acme-retail returned no tokens for ~90s and then resumed. Customer-facing impact: one checkout flow experienced a hang and retry.

What we have so far:
- Request IDs (from our side): req_20271007_5781, req_20271007_5784, req_20271007_5789
- Approx window: 2027-10-07T03:15:30Z -> 2027-10-07T03:17:00Z
- Model: redwood-3b-v2 (quantized), via hosted API in us-west region
- We captured a packet capture and logs (attached minimalized versions).

Can you confirm whether there was any platform-level throttling, model stall, or known deployment event? This hit production traffic so we need a short RCA for the ops team and a note for the customer.

Thanks,
Samir
Tess Hsu (on-call)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.example>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acmeretail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.example, marcus.lin@redwood.example
Date: 2027-10-07T04:03:29Z
Subject: Re: Observed ~90s silence on streaming completions (03:15–03:17 UTC)

Samir — thanks for the quick heads up and the request IDs.

We're starting triage now. Can you confirm whether the SDK reported any client-side timeouts/reconnects for those request IDs, and whether your proxy logs show TCP resets? Also: did you see any repeated zero-byte responses or just a pause followed by normal tokens?

We'll pull platform traces, model metrics, and network telemetry for the same window. I have Marcus on deck for model/runtime checks and Marissa to help correlate infra events.

Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: pcap-snippet-0315.txt (pcap summary)
Attachment: request_ids_0315.csv (CSV list)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.example>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.example; marissa.cole@redwood.example
Date: 2027-10-07T07:10:54Z
Subject: Re: Observed ~90s silence on streaming completions (03:15–03:17 UTC)

Quick notes from infra/model side (initial pass):
- No control-plane deployments or host recycling in us-west during 03:10–03:25 UTC.
- GPU telemetry for the host pools serving redwood-3b-v2 shows normal utilization (no OOM or kernel stalls).
- Our streaming-layer logs for req_20271007_5781/5784/5789 show the requests reached the runtime and the kernel produced token batches; there are no internal errors or retries recorded.
- KV cache lookups and prefix-cache entries look normal.
- We attempted an in-region replay using the same model, batch shape, and payloads (sanitized). No reproduce: the replayed streams returned tokens continuously.

Hypothesis: client-proxy/network blackout or an intermediate TCP stall causing zero bytes to reach client even though server continued producing.

Next steps proposed:
1) Ask Acme for client-side SDK logs showing socket state & any HTTP chunk boundaries during the window.
2) Provide guidance: increase socket read timeout to 120s and enable our request debug header to capture chunk offsets if this happens again.
3) Keep the thread open for 48h for any additional evidence.

Marcus
SRE — Serving Runtime

From: Samir Patel <samir@acmeretail.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.example; marissa.cole@redwood.example; marcus.lin@redwood.example
Date: 2027-10-07T09:40:11Z
Subject: Re: Observed ~90s silence on streaming completions (03:15–03:17 UTC)

Thanks — attaching our SDK debug logs (trimmed) and the proxy edge logs. We see the client socket remained ESTABLISHED and then a burst of retransmits from our edge during the window. Also attaching the request_ids CSV.

We can accept the 48h monitoring window; if you need any additional captures we can coordinate a debug window tonight.

Attachments: acme_logs_subset_20271007.zip

—Samir

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.example>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acmeretail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.example, marcus.lin@redwood.example
Date: 2027-10-08T11:22:05Z
Subject: Final update — no platform correlation found (summary & recommendations)

Samir / Tess — thanks for the logs and patience while we investigated. Summary of findings: 

- Investigation window: 2027-10-07T03:10:00Z -> 2027-10-07T03:25:00Z.
- Platform control plane: no deploys, host recycling, or autoscale events.
- Serving runtime: requests reached the runtime and produced token batches; we have continuous produce metrics with no internal retries or model stalls for the request IDs you provided.
- Network telemetry: between client edge and our edge we see packet loss/retransmit spikes in your provided pcap snippet during the 03:15–03:17 UTC window; internal network (within our cloud provider) shows no correlated packet loss.

Conclusion: We were unable to reproduce a server-side stall or platform-caused interruption. The evidence is most consistent with an edge / client-network transient (packet retransmits causing the appearance of a silent stream at the client).

Recommended mitigation actions for Acme Retail (short-term):
- Increase client read/socket timeout to 120s to avoid premature client-side retries.
- Implement client-side idempotent retry logic for streaming completions (reconnect + resume where possible).
- Enable Redwood debug header (X-Rwd-Debug: 1) for a short debug window so we can capture chunk offsets and HTTP/2 frame boundaries if this recurs.
- Share any future pcap captures and SDK logs immediately and keep request IDs handy.

We will leave monitoring on for 48 hours; if you see recurrence please open a new thread with fresh captures and we will re-prioritize.

If you'd like, we can schedule a short joint debug call to walk network teams through what to look for.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: acme_logs_subset_20271007.zip, pcap-snippet-0315.txt, request_ids_0315.csv

Note: thread closed from Redwood side for active investigation. If new evidence appears we will re-open and escalate as needed.
